label: harness-contract-violation
rationale: Re-graded, not inferred. I rebuilt the grading host in two variants — the current `scripts/memory-host.mjs`, which hands every session ONE frozen facade, and a copy patched back to the pre-repair behaviour that rebuilt the facade per session over the same store — and ran this preserved `submission/subject.mjs` through both against the same 288-scenario measured set, scoring with the family's own `verify()`. Under the per-session facade the result reproduces the recorded cells EXACTLY (32 failing scenarios, the identical scenario ids, `audit_explains` + `no_forbidden_call`); under the one-facade host it is 0/288. The submission depends on facade identity at `const memoryMeta = new WeakMap()` with `stateFor(memory)` returning a fresh `{ byKey: new Map() }` whenever the facade is not the one it saw last, so a fresh facade per session wiped its cross-session bookkeeping at every boundary. That dependency is legitimate: `challenge/README.md` and `challenge/types.ts` both publish "called once per session, in order, with the SAME memory facade throughout", and `test/memory-facade-contract.test.ts` now pins that identity as a contract. Note the failures sit entirely at sessionsBetween 1 and 3 and are zero at 0, which is the signature of a defect that can only bite at a session boundary. This trial failed BECAUSE it believed the published contract, so `harness-contract-violation` and specifically NOT `capability`.
